questions.q: Which prominent Nigerian artist is universally recognized as the 'Father of Modern Nigerian Art'?
questions.explain: Chief Aina Onabolu is celebrated as the pioneer of modern art in Nigeria, being the first to advocate for formal art education and producing realistic portrait paintings.
questions.exam: BECE Cultural & Creative Arts: Nigerian Art Heritage & Pioneers

questions.topic: Efforts of some Pioneering Nigerian Artists

questions.q: Aina Onabolu's major contribution to the development of Nigerian art, aside from his portrait paintings, was:
options: Introducing art as a subject into the Nigerian school curriculum.
Inventing the lost-wax bronze casting method.
Establishing the National Theatre in Lagos.
Creating the first Nigerian currency notes.
questions.explain: Aina Onabolu fiercely advocated for formal art education, leading to the introduction of Fine Arts into the curriculum of Nigerian schools by colonial administrators.
questions.exam: BECE Cultural & Creative Arts: Nigerian Art Heritage & Pioneers
questions.subject: Arts
questions.topic: Efforts of some Pioneering Nigerian Artists

questions.q: Akinola Lasekan was another pioneer in contemporary Nigerian art. Which artistic genres was he most famous for?
questions.explain: Akinola Lasekan was a pioneering contemporary artist known for his realistic portrait paintings and for being one of Nigeria's first political cartoonists during the nationalist struggles.
questions.exam: BECE Cultural & Creative Arts: Nigerian Art Heritage & Pioneers

questions.topic: Efforts of some Pioneering Nigerian Artists

questions.q: Ladi Kwali gained international recognition for her exceptional skills in which field of art?
questions.explain: Dr. Ladi Kwali was a master potter whose beautiful ceramic works blending traditional Gwari techniques with modern pottery styles gained her global fame.

questions.q: To honor Ladi Kwali's immense contribution to Nigerian arts, an image of her engaged in her craft is featured on which Nigerian currency?
questions.explain: Ladi Kwali is famously depicted making pottery on the reverse side of the Nigerian 20 Naira note.
questions.exam: BECE Cultural & Creative Arts: Nigerian Art Heritage & Pioneers

questions.q: Bruce Onabrakpeya is an internationally acclaimed Nigerian artist primarily known for his innovative techniques in which field of art?
questions.explain: Bruce Onabrakpeya is highly celebrated for his printmaking, specifically pioneering techniques like plastography and etching.
questions.exam: BECE Cultural & Creative Arts: Nigerian Art Heritage & Pioneers

questions.topic: Efforts of some Pioneering Nigerian Artists

questions.q: Lamidi Fakeye, a renowned contemporary artist, heavily influenced modern art using traditional Yoruba methods in which artistic medium?
questions.explain: Lamidi Fakeye was a globally recognized neo-traditional Yoruba wood carver who sculpted intricate wooden figures and pillars blending modern themes with traditional Yoruba artistic principles.

questions.q: Etsu Ngbodaga (Clara Etso Ugbodaga-Ngu) holds a significant place in Nigerian art history primarily as:
options: The first Nigerian to sculpt in bronze.
A pioneering female painter and art educator who taught at the Nigerian College of Arts, Zaria.
The architect who designed the National Museum.
The creator of the Nok terracotta heads.
questions.explain: Clara Etso Ugbodaga-Ngu (sometimes written as Etsu Ngbodaga) was a trailblazing female Nigerian artist and the first indigenous art educator at the influential Nigerian College of Arts, Science and Technology in Zaria.
questions.exam: BECE Cultural & Creative Arts: Nigerian Art Heritage & Pioneers

questions.topic: Efforts of some Pioneering Nigerian Artists

questions.q: Chief Aina Onabolu is renowned in Nigerian art history primarily for his mastery of which artistic style?
questions.explain: Aina Onabolu was the first African painter to master the techniques of Western academic art, painting highly realistic portraits to prove that Africans were capable of producing fine art at the same level as Europeans.
questions.exam: BECE Cultural & Creative Arts: Nigerian Art Heritage & Pioneers

questions.q: Alongside his painting, Akinola Lasekan made significant contributions to Nigerian history through what specific medium during the nationalist era?
options: Drawing powerful political cartoons for anti-colonial newspapers
Weaving the first modern Aso-Oke textiles
questions.explain: Akinola Lasekan used his artistic talent as a tool for social commentary, becoming famous for his political cartoons in nationalist newspapers (like Nnamdi Azikiwe's West African Pilot) which criticized British colonial rule.

questions.q: In 1956, Queen Elizabeth II commissioned a bronze portrait of herself. Which pioneering Nigerian artist sculpted this historic piece?
questions.explain: Ben Enwonwu's international recognition peaked when he was commissioned to sculpt a bronze statue of Queen Elizabeth II during her visit to Nigeria in 1956, making him the first African artist to receive such a royal commission.
questions.exam: BECE Cultural & Creative Arts: Nigerian Art Heritage & Pioneers
questions.subject: Arts
questions.topic: Efforts of some Pioneering Nigerian Artists

questions.q: Clara Etso Ugbodaga-Ngu (Etsu Ngbodaga) was a pivotal figure in contemporary Nigerian art due to her role as:
options: The sole designer of the FESTAC '77 mask
The first female indigenous art lecturer at the Nigerian College of Arts, Zaria
The founder of the Osogbo Art School
A traditional cloth weaver in Kano
questions.explain: Clara Ugbodaga-Ngu was a trailblazing female artist and educator. She taught many of the legendary 'Zaria Rebels' as the first Nigerian female lecturer in the Fine Arts department at Zaria.

questions.q: Which globally renowned Nigerian contemporary artist is primarily famous for mastering the 'Plastograph' and 'Deep Etching' techniques in printmaking?
questions.explain: Bruce Onabrakpeya is a master printmaker who innovated several printmaking techniques, including plastography and deep etching, producing heavily textured and colorful prints reflecting Nigerian folklore.

questions.q: Dr. Ladi Kwali's globally acclaimed artworks are characterized by large water pots decorated with incised geometric patterns and animal motifs like lizards and scorpions. What art form did she practice?
questions.explain: Ladi Kwali was an iconic Nigerian potter. Working at the Abuja Pottery Training Centre with Michael Cardew, she elevated traditional Gwari hand-built pottery into globally recognized ceramic art.
questions.exam: BECE Cultural & Creative Arts: Nigerian Art Heritage & Pioneers

questions.q: Which pioneer artist was an internationally recognized neo-traditional Yoruba wood carver who sculpted intricate wooden posts and doors for universities and churches?
questions.explain: Lamidi Fakeye descended from a long line of Yoruba wood carvers. He adapted traditional Yoruba carving styles (like those seen on palace pillars and doors) to contemporary themes and public commissions.

questions.q: Yusuf Grillo, a prominent contemporary painter and Zaria Rebel, is well known for his distinct painting style characterized by what?
options: Hyper-realistic portraits using only black and white
Elongated, stylized figures painted in cool, monochromatic blue hues
Large, aggressive splatters of red paint
Miniature watercolor paintings of wild animals
questions.explain: Yusuf Grillo's signature style involves mathematically stylized, elongated human figures often clothed in Yoruba attire, painted using a distinct, serene palette heavily dominated by the color blue.

questions.q: In his mission to prove African capabilities to the British colonial masters, Aina Onabolu refused to paint:
questions.explain: Colonial administrators believed Africans were only capable of primitive or stylized crafts. To prove them wrong, Aina Onabolu deliberately rejected abstract art and mastered strict Western photographic realism in his portraits.
questions.exam: BECE Cultural & Creative Arts: Nigerian Art Heritage & Pioneers

questions.topic: Efforts of some Pioneering Nigerian Artists

questions.q: Bruce Onabrakpeya’s artwork is heavily inspired by the folklore, myths, and legends of which Nigerian ethnic group?
questions.explain: Hailing from Delta State, Bruce Onabrakpeya frequently incorporates Urhobo myths, folklore, and visual motifs into his highly stylized prints and paintings.
